players.product: Large-scale liquid-cooled AI data-center campuses (Polaris Forge / Delta Forge)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter ended August 31, 2026), per CFO Saidal Mohmand: total revenue $341.9 million, up 322% from $80.9 million in the prior-year quarter. HPC Hosting Business revenue $262.6 million, consisting of $65.8 million of base rent, $183.5 million of tenant fit-out services and $13.3 million of tenant recoveries. Data Center Hosting Business (the two Bitcoin hosting sites) revenue $37.8 million, in line with the prior-year quarter, generating $13.3 million of operating profit on approximately $111.9 million of segment assets; segment operating profit more than doubled from $6 million in the prior quarter, driven by favorable power pricing. ChronoScale revenue (consolidated in GAAP, excluded from non-GAAP) was $41.5 million, including approximately $23 million of GPU hardware sales.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $341.9 million, up 322% from $80.9 million; HPC Hosting $262.6 million (base rent $65.8 million, tenant fit-out $183.5 million, tenant recoveries $13.3 million); Data Center Hosting $37.8 million; ChronoScale $41.5 million

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q1 2027 profitability and cost detail from the CFO: adjusted EBITDA $64.4 million, up from $500,000 in the prior-year quarter; net operating income (exclusive to the HPC Hosting Business) $58.8 million, an 89% margin; net loss from continuing operations attributable to common stockholders $221 million or $0.76 per share; adjusted net loss $4.1 million or $0.01 per diluted share. Services and other cost of revenues $245.7 million, primarily $176.1 million of tenant fit-out services in the HPC Hosting Business, $22.4 million associated with ChronoScale's GPU hardware sales, $19.8 million in energy cost and $17.6 million in depreciation and amortization. Data center rental and other cost of revenues $43.9 million, including $22.4 million of depreciation and amortization on the operational AI factories at Polaris Forge 1. SG&A $114.7 million, including $65.4 million of stock-based compensation ($41.3 million tied to one-time performance stock units). The quarter also recorded a $67.5 million non-cash loss from the change in fair value of the Babcock & Wilcox warrants and common stock investment. Quarter end: approximately $2.9 billion in cash and cash equivalents plus $0.7 billion of restricted cash, against approximately $6.4 billion of debt; stockholders' equity approximately $1.6 billion. CEO: the Data Center Hosting Business's 286 MW of capacity for Bitcoin mining across two North Dakota sites provides steady, high-margin revenue with minimal ongoing capital investment.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBITDA $64.4 million; NOI $58.8 million (89% margin); net loss $221 million or $0.76 per share; adjusted net loss $4.1 million; $67.5 million non-cash loss on Babcock & Wilcox warrants and stock; cash approximately $2.9 billion, debt approximately $6.4 billion; 286 MW Bitcoin mining hosting capacity

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Wes Cummins: Applied Digital has approximately $36 billion in contracted revenue across five campuses, three states and two very different geographic regions; the near- to medium-term focus shifts from growing contracted value to converting the contracted portfolio and bringing contracted capacity online. It targets take-or-pay contracts of at least 15 years with proven tier-one investment-grade hyperscalers. CFO: Polaris Forge 3, Delta Forge 1 and Delta Forge 2 are all leased to the same tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler under 15-year take-or-pay leases. CEO: the company has three customers in North Dakota and is being more selective with the customers it builds for, on credit quality, because it has a limited amount of capacity to build.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $36 billion contracted revenue across five campuses; Polaris Forge 3, Delta Forge 1, Delta Forge 2 on 15-year take-or-pay leases with one tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (CEO): over the next 12 months Applied Digital expects to place over 600 MW into service, versus 250 MW over the past 12 months. With the expected initial operation of the Harwood, North Dakota campus, it anticipates having 300 MW of total critical IT online across North Dakota by the end of this calendar year. Revenue contribution from the Louisiana and Alabama campuses is expected to begin in the first half of calendar year 2027. The CFO expects the first building at Polaris Forge 2 to be on track and on budget.
quarterly_data.figure: over 600 MW into service over the next 12 months (vs 250 MW over the past 12 months); 300 MW critical IT online across North Dakota by end of calendar year; Louisiana / Alabama revenue from 1H calendar 2027

capex.display: over 600 MW into service over the next 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: Long-term target (CEO): if demand continues on its current path and the company keeps executing, he believes Applied Digital can grow its operating portfolio to 3.5 GW-4 GW by the end of calendar year 2030. He says the power for this is in the pipeline (including the additional Base Electron capacity coming in 2030) and the target is mainly about how far build and delivery can ramp: the high end implies delivering about 1 GW per year in 2029 and 2030 after a bridge to around 2 GW by the end of calendar year 2028, which the company thinks is the level it can ramp construction and delivery to.
quarterly_data.figure: 3.5 GW-4 GW operating portfolio by end of calendar year 2030; around 2 GW by end of calendar year 2028; about 1 GW per year in 2029 and 2030 at the high end

quarterly_data.signal: Expansion leases (CEO): Applied Digital currently expects approximately 250 MW of expansion leases at existing campuses to be executed by calendar year-end at materially higher pricing than prior leases; he fully expects lease expansions and new campuses at materially higher rates than the contracts signed in the first half of 2026. Asked to define premium pricing, he says the company is pushing for 'definitely north of 15%+ increases on the lease rate', which could also include longer lease duration, without wanting to pin that down.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 250 MW of expansion leases expected by calendar year-end; north of 15%+ lease-rate increases targeted

quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain and power (CEO): power remains the single largest gating factor in the industry. Supply chain is tight across the industry, some components more so than others. Almost two years ago Applied Digital locked in key components with certain suppliers - in some instances purchasing full factory capacity output from certain factories for, he believes, a four-year timeframe - and it is pushing to upsize that amount because it expects to need more supply chain in 2027, 2028 and 2029 to build to the demand it sees.
quarterly_data.figure: full factory capacity output purchased from certain factories for a four-year timeframe (as the CEO believes)

quarterly_data.signal: Power in North Dakota (CEO): Applied Digital entered into a long-term power purchase agreement with Base Electron, an independent power producer in which it holds an approximate 10% equity stake, covering an approximately 1,200-MW natural gas facility Base Electron is developing in central North Dakota adjacent to the Polaris Forge 3 campus, with deliveries expected to begin in 2030; the agreement can follow Applied Digital's tenants. He expects Base Electron to build significant capacity on the eastern side of the state to help expand the Harwood campus, and potentially around Jamestown. A new WBI pipeline (WBI is owned by MDU) has been approved; Applied Digital will be a gas offtaker at Center and Harwood for certain and possibly Jamestown, with almost unlimited expansion capacity at Center; this will all be front-of-the-meter and grid-connected. CEO: 'we're looking at procured equipment that's roughly 2.4 GW-2.5 GW of generation capacity there already', expected to go significantly larger. At Harwood, Applied Digital paid for over $100 million of substation and grid upgrades itself, and MDU's customers have saved about $45 million since the Ellendale project began.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 1,200-MW natural gas facility, deliveries expected to begin in 2030; approximately 10% equity stake; roughly 2.4 GW-2.5 GW of procured generation equipment; over $100 million Harwood substation and grid upgrades
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: independent power producer and power purchase agreement counterparty, approximately 10% owned by Applied Digital

quarterly_data.signal: Finland (CEO): Applied Digital signed an agreement for up to 1 GW of potential power capacity in Finland, described as a measured first step outside the United States, while near-term priorities remain US execution. The company purchased the site after looking at probably 30-40 sites over about 12 months; the first 100 MW is available in 2028, ramping through 2031 to the full gigawatt, with additional payments at later power break points and an off-ramp before those payments. The site is about 30 km from a self-build of one of the large hyperscalers, and existing and potential customers have started asking more about European capacity in the last four months. Build cost is expected to be roughly the same in dollars as in the US, with a more elongated delivery timeline.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 1 GW potential power capacity; first 100 MW available in 2028; full gigawatt through 2031

quarterly_data.signal: ChronoScale (approximately 96% owned): during the quarter ChronoScale announced plans with Microsoft for a 50-MW AI compute deployment in North America featuring NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, which the CEO says is expected to significantly expand ChronoScale's business with a tier-one investment-grade customer. CEO: with recent new contracts ChronoScale is on track to reach $1 billion of ARR in 2027. Strategy: ChronoScale secures data center capacity outside the large-scale Applied Digital sites, at 50-MW to 100-MW grid-tied sites and through smaller modular builds; the CEO thinks ChronoScale could move up to multiple hundreds of megawatts of capacity online over 2027 and 2028. The CEO also cited NVIDIA's expectation that neoclouds exit this year with 8 GW of installed capacity, up from 3 GW at the end of 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Microsoft 50-MW deployment (NVIDIA GB300 NVL72); $1 billion ARR in 2027 on track; approximately 96% ownership
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: customer of ChronoScale (Applied Digital's approximately 96%-owned GPU cloud subsidiary)

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and market (CEO): demand 'remains extremely robust right now' - 'it feels like we are at max' - with customers still pushing for 2027 capacity; almost everything in 2027 should be fairly contracted, Applied Digital has capacity contracted into 2028, and it sees a lot of demand for 2028 and 2029. In North Dakota he is aware of a roughly 1 GW self-build project by one of the tier-one hyperscalers and is in multiple conversations with other tier-one hyperscalers for additional capacity. He says growing local moratoriums, tighter zoning and longer permitting increase the scarcity value of campuses already powered and community-supported, supporting expansions, renewals and renewal pricing. On workloads: over the past 18 months the tenant (technical) fit-out has become a larger dollar amount and much more flexible, as customers build in flexibility for GPU / TPU, CPU mix, storage and network topology. Its fourth-generation data center design is built for 30+ year horizons rather than a five- to six-year GPU life cycle.
quarterly_data.figure: roughly 1 GW tier-one hyperscaler self-build in North Dakota; 2027 capacity fairly contracted; capacity contracted into 2028

connects_to.relationship: Polaris Forge 1 — 400 MW dedicated AI data-center campus leased to CoreWeave (North Dakota)

contracts.signal: CEO: Applied Digital signed its first lease with CoreWeave in May of 2025 for the first two buildings at Polaris Forge 1; the first building was fully operational by the end of calendar 2025, capable of supporting more than 40,000 liquid-cooled NVIDIA GB300s, and the second became operational approximately one year after breaking ground in summer 2025. Polaris Forge 1 has now achieved full ready for service across its first two buildings, encompassing 10 data halls supported by 250 MW of critical IT load (a 150% increase in delivered capacity), with the third building progressing on schedule. CEO: 'CoreWeave's a great customer'.
contracts.units: 250 MW critical IT load operational across 10 data halls (first two buildings); more than 40,000 liquid-cooled NVIDIA GB300s in the first building
